chunks: In what I think [is narrated] from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: Abu Dharr (may God be pleased with him) was seen watering a donkey at al-Rabadha. So some of the people said to him: 'Is there no one, O Abu Dharr, who could water the donkey for you?'

He said: 'I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) saying: There is no animal except that it asks God every morning: O God, grant me a righteous owner who will feed me until I am full, give me water until I am quenched, and not burden me beyond my strength. So I love to water it myself.'

key_terms.الرَّبَذَة: Al-Rabadha, a small settlement in the Arabian Peninsula near Medina where Abu Dharr was exiled by Caliph Uthman
key_terms.دَابَّة: Any land animal, especially a riding or working beast; here indicating that all animals universally share this supplication
key_terms.طَاقَة: Capacity, strength, endurance; the animal's threshold beyond which work becomes oppression
key_terms.مَلِيك صَالِح: Righteous owner/master; one who fulfills their animal's needs without cruelty or overwork

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about how animals pray for their owners?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an encounter with Abu Dharr al-Ghifari during his exile at al-Rabadha, where he was personally tending his donkey. When questioned about this humble act, he cited a prophetic narration that all animals supplicate daily for a righteous, compassionate master. This story highlights the Islamic ethic of kind treatment of animals, rooted in the Prophet's teachings, and Abu Dharr's exemplary implementation of this principle even in his circumstances of poverty and exile.
word_analysis: suffices you/takes care of it for you

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Al Magra, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said regarding what I think is, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Abu Zarr<sup>ra</sup> was seen watering a donkey at Al-Rabza, so one of the people said to him<sup>ra</sup>, ‘Is there not for you<sup>as</sup>, O Abu Zarr<sup>ra</sup>, one who would water the donkey for you<sup>as</sup>?’

So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘I<sup>ra</sup> heard Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> saying: ‘There is none from the animals except that it asks Allah<sup>azwj</sup> every morning, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Grant me a righteous owner who would satiate me from the feed, and would quench me from the water, and would not encumber me above my strength’. Therefore I<sup>ra</sup> love to water it myself<sup>ra</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from abu al-Mighra’ from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has said the following as I thing from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that abu Dharr was seen offering water to a donkey at al- Rabadhah and certain people said to him, ‘O abu Dharr do you not have someone who can offer water to your donkey?’

He said, ‘I once heard the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, saying, “Every stumper asks Allah every morning, ‘O Lord, grant me an owner who will feed me sufficiently of feed, offer me water, will not load me more than my power.’” For this reason I personally offer it water.’”
